memory_lessons.applicability: Useful for prioritizing further weighted-sum work, but the recorded cases do not establish behavior on all numerical edge cases.
memory_lessons.claim: The baseline measured 0.390079 s. Two distinct weighted-sum programs were controller-valid on eight reported cases at 0.160145 s and 0.076580 s; the faster reported maximum absolute error was 2.0981e-4. These are measurements of prior programs, not this candidate.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this endpoint-anchored weight recurrence against the same baseline and run every available correctness case without changing tolerance.

proposal.hypothesis: The two measured weighted-sum variants reduced mean latency from 0.390079 s to 0.160145 s and 0.076580 s, respectively. This candidate tests whether generating binomial weights by a recurrence from the dominant endpoint (rather than repeated per-term power work) lowers the remaining cost while limiting tail underflow. It preserves 63 discounts and terminal indices j=0..63; performance and edge-case correctness remain unmeasured.

retained: Replace the 63-stage triangular recurrence in the ordinary probability domain with its equivalent weighted sum using C(63,j) weights and exactly 63 discount factors.
Generate terminal values only for j=0..63 with exponents 2*j-64, using one double-precision starting power and sequential multiplication by u squared.
Generate binomial weights from the dominant endpoint and accumulate in double precision; retain the baseline recurrence for out-of-domain probabilities and non-finite or non-positive u.
